headline: High: open-webui can ingest and forward content via MCP/files while Superset can act on analytics inputs, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui exposes MCP, OpenAPI tool servers, plugins, and file inputs, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction-following path. Superset is a downstream analytics app that may consume outputs or artifacts from open-webui, making indirect injection plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF open-webui ingests untrusted documents or web content through MCP/plugins/files and forwards them to Superset workflows
IF Superset renders or reuses open-webui-generated text without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP/plugins for untrusted sources
Require explicit human review before copying open-webui output into Superset
Tag imported content with source provenance
Restrict open-webui file access to a dedicated folder
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui touches API keys, documents, chat messages, files, and persistent memory, and it has broad network egress plus cloud/API integrations. Superset is allowlisted-network and can receive analytics data; if shared workspace or copied artifacts exist, sensitive content can flow from open-webui into Superset outputs or logs. The blast radius includes secrets and documents, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF open-webui stores API keys, documents, or chat messages that are then exported into Superset dashboards or queries
IF both agents share a filesystem, mounted volume, or copied artifacts containing sensitive data
mitigations: Separate workspaces and mounted volumes
Remove secrets from open-webui before any export
Limit Superset datasets to non-sensitive tables
Turn off broad egress where possible
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on the handoff path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui can write local files, use mounted volumes, spawn subprocesses, and make broad network calls; Superset can make allowlisted network calls. Even without explicit write permissions in Superset, overlapping access to shared resources or APIs can cause conflicts if both operate on the same data products. Uncertainty about shared mutable state pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same mounted volume or shared dataset
IF open-webui subprocesses modify artifacts that Superset reads or refreshes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Use read-only mounts for Superset inputs
Schedule writes and refreshes at different times
Lock shared datasets during updates
requires-engineering: add coordination/locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can generate and transform content that Superset may consume as analytics input or displayed text. Superset is not documented here as critically verifying upstream outputs, so a mistaken or malicious open-webui result could propagate into dashboards or decisions. The pathway exists in default-style integrations, but the blast radius is usually bounded to reports and work products.
conditions: IF Superset ingests open-webui-generated summaries, SQL, or annotations without verification
IF downstream users treat those outputs as authoritative
mitigations: Add a verification step before ingestion
Require source links for every imported claim
Mark open-webui outputs as untrusted by default
Review dashboards after each refresh
requires-engineering: implement validation rules for imported content

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, chat messages, usage analytics, and persistent memory, while Superset is a separate open-source analytics system with no stated retention or residency controls in the profile. If regulated data is moved from open-webui into Superset, mismatched logging or retention policies can create compliance gaps. I cannot prove a residency violation, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF regulated documents, chat messages, or API keys from open-webui are loaded into Superset
IF Superset retention or logging exceeds the source system's policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Superset
Review retention settings in both systems
Disable verbose query logging for sensitive datasets
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems
